subject: Zero-downtime cert swap + split-zone routing for private hostnames
messages:
From: Alice Moran <alice.moran@acme-corp.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, platform-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2028-07-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Cert rotation for private hostnames behind VPC/VPN

Hi Jonas (and platform ops),

We're planning a CA/leaf certificate rotation for our private hostnames (notably freight-api.acme.internal and admin.acme.internal) that are reachable via VPC peering and our on-prem VPN. Our PKI team wants to move to a new intermediate CA and rotate leaf certs over the next two weeks.

Primary asks:
- Can Redwood support a zero-downtime cert swap for private endpoints that are terminated at your private edge (customer private endpoint option)?
- What changes do you expect on our split-horizon DNS (internal resolver vs on-prem resolvers) to avoid traffic blackholes during the swap?
- How does OCSP/CRL behavior look for clients on-prem vs clients in our cloud VPC?

We have a short list of FQDNs and current expiry dates — attached (cert inventory). Would appreciate a short runbook or checklist you can execute with us. We'd like a canary rollout (50 sessions/users) before broad rotation.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Moran
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Logistics

Subject: Re: Cert rotation for private hostnames behind VPC/VPN

Alice — thanks for the heads-up. We can definitely support a rotation with zero customer-visible downtime, but we need to coordinate DNS and termination points carefully. High-level checklist I propose: 

1) Inventory confirmation: full list of FQDNs + current SANs and chain (please confirm attached CSV).
2) Decide termination topology: edge-terminated (Redwood private endpoint proxy) vs customer-side termination (on-prem proxy).
3) Dual-present certs strategy: present both old and new cert chains (via SNI mapping) during canary phase so existing sessions continue while new clients validate new chain.
4) Split-horizon DNS plan: ensure on-prem resolver and VPC resolver can independently switch VIPs (or TTLs) so we can steer a percentage of traffic to the canary pool.
5) OCSP/CRL check plan: confirm that your internal clients can reach OCSP responders or use stapling on the edge.
6) Canary execution window + rollback criteria.

I'll loop in Karthik for the nitty-gritty on proxy config and DNS cutover steps. If you can confirm a preferred maintenance window (timezone: CET) and the absolute latest expiry date, we can produce a one-page runbook and schedule the canary.

-Jonas

Subject: Re: Cert rotation for private hostnames behind VPC/VPN — proposed technical plan

On Tue, Jul 17, 2028 at 11:03 AM jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alice — thanks for the heads-up. We can definitely support a rotation with zero customer-visible downtime...

Hi all — putting forward a concrete, low-risk approach we've used successfully with other private deployments. Key ideas: dual-serving + SNI selector + split DNS steering.

Summary (high level):
- Create new leaf certs signed by your new intermediate CA that include: the existing SANs + an explicit SAN alias used only for the canary (e.g., freight-api.canary.acme.internal).
- Deploy the new cert chain to a separate canary pool of Redwood private endpoints (we can create one ephemeral pool per your account).
- Configure the private edge proxy to present cert chain A for SNI X and cert chain B for SNI Y. During the canary, the proxy will present the new chain only to connections routed to the canary pool. Old sessions on the main pool will continue to use the old cert.
- Split-horizon DNS: update your internal resolver to add a low-ttl A record for freight-api.acme.internal that points to both the main VIP and the canary VIP (weighted A records or service endpoints). Your on-prem resolver can be updated to point a small percentage of clients to the canary VIP by providing a specific view or A record override.
- OCSP/Stapling: we recommend enabling stapling on Redwood's private edge for the new chain; this removes dependence on clients reaching external OCSP responders. Ensure your OCSP responder is reachable from Redwood's private control plane (we can coordinate connectivity test).
- Client cert pinning / mTLS: if you use client cert pinning, plan to accept both old and new client certs at the backend for a brief overlap window, or issue a short-lived bridging client cert.

Step-by-step (short):
1) You issue the new leaf certs (CSR guidance attached) with both existing FQDNs and the canary alias.
2) Redwood uploads the new cert chain into your private certificate store and deploys to a canary pool.
3) Update on-prem DNS view to return canary VIP for a small subset of IP ranges (we can provide sample zone entries).
4) Verify TLS handshake and OCSP stapled responses against sample clients (we'll run tests with curl + openssl s_client as part of the checklist).
5) Run canary for 2 hours, monitor errors and latency; if OK, expand percentage in 2x increments until 100%.
6) After full swap, revoke old leaf certs and tidy DNS TTLs back to normal.

Risks and mitigations:
- OCSP reachability: mitigate with stapling and a short-lived bridging OCSP cache on your side.
- Split-horizon divergence: prepare a rollback zone file to revert A records if issues arise.
- Client pinning issues: include a fallback header-based routing rule for known clients.

I've attached a one-page playbook (cert-rotation-playbook-v1.pdf) and a csv with proposed zone mappings (dns-zone-mapping.csv). Happy to jump on a short call to walk the runbook step-by-step.

-Karthik

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with our internal PKI team's thinking. A few clarifications from our side:

- OCSP: we'll enable stapling in our OCSP responder and open the necessary egress paths from Redwood's control plane — working with infra to confirm reachability.
- Canary scope: yes to 50 sessions initially. We'd like the canary to be restricted to a handful of build agents and our internal web portal users (IP ranges 10.24.0.0/22 and 10.24.128.0/22).
- Window: can you do the canary on 2028-07-20 between 06:00–09:00 CET? Our PKI lead says leaf certs expire 2028-08-02 so we need to finish by 07-31 at the latest.

Please confirm the timeline and whether Redwood will manage the edge-side stapling configuration and health checks. Also, we want a short incident rollback procedure in the runbook with DNS zone snapshots.

Alice

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Alice — we can take the canary on 2028-07-20 06:00–09:00 CET. Confirmed actions from Redwood:
- Redwood will deploy the new chain to a canary endpoint pool and enable TLS stapling on that pool.
- We'll run the health checks and live TLS handshake tests (we will provide the script and the expected outputs).
- We'll coordinate with your infra to apply the on-prem zone override for the two IP ranges you listed.

I've uploaded the one-page runbook and an executable checklist; please find links below. We will also capture a DNS zone snapshot before each change and keep a rollback button in the console. If anything crosses the error thresholds in the canary (5xx > 1% or latency P95 +50ms), we will revert to the old pool and DNS snapshot immediately.

Action items:
- Alice: confirm final CSR files and that OCSP stapling endpoint is reachable from Redwood control plane by 2028-07-19 18:00 CET.
- Acme infra: apply on-prem DNS view change at canary start time (we can provide sample zone entries).
- Redwood (Karthik/Jonas): execute canary, monitor, expand, revoke old certs.

I'll send an invite for a 30-minute pre-cutover sync tomorrow.

Best,
